title: Motion in a Straight Line
syllabus: Frame of reference, Motion in a straight line: Position-time graph, speed and velocity; Uniform and non-uniform motion, average speed and instantaneous velocity; Uniformly accelerated motion, velocity-time and position-time graphs, relations for uniformly accelerated motion; Free fall under gravity; Relative velocity in one dimension

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A car covers the first half of the distance between two places at $40\text{ km/h}$ and the remaining half at $60\text{ km/h}$. The average speed of the car is:
questions.solution:
For two equal halves of distance traveled at speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$, average speed is the harmonic mean:
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = \frac{2 \times 40 \times 60}{40 + 60} = \frac{4800}{100} = 48\text{ km/h}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle starts from rest and moves with acceleration $a$ which varies with time as $a = 3t + 4\text{ m/s}^2$. The velocity of the particle at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Acceleration is $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 3t + 4$.
Integrating with initial condition $v(0) = 0$:
$$v = \int_0^2 (3t + 4)\,dt = \left[ \frac{3t^2}{2} + 4t \right]_0^2 = \frac{3(4)}{2} + 4(2) = 6 + 8 = 14\text{ m/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of $19.6\text{ m/s}$ from the top of a tower. The ball strikes the ground after $6\text{ s}$. The height of the tower is (take $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
Taking upward direction as positive:
$u = +19.6\text{ m/s}$, $a = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, $t = 6\text{ s}$.
Using the displacement relation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$:
$$s = (19.6)(6) - \frac{1}{2}(9.8)(6)^2 = 117.6 - 4.9(36) = 117.6 - 176.4 = -58.8\text{ m}$$
Height of tower $h = |s| = 58.8\text{ m}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A bullet loses $\frac{1}{20}$ of its velocity in passing through a wooden plank. The least number of such identical planks required to stop the bullet completely is:
questions.solution:
Let initial velocity be $u$ and thickness of one plank be $x$.
Velocity after passing through one plank is $v = u - \frac{u}{20} = \frac{19}{20}u$.
Using $v^2 - u^2 = 2ax$:
$$\left(\frac{19}{20}u\right)^2 - u^2 = 2ax \implies 2ax = -u^2\left(1 - \frac{361}{400}\right) = -\frac{39}{400}u^2$$
If $n$ planks stop the bullet ($v_f = 0$ after distance $nx$):
$$0^2 - u^2 = 2a(nx) = n(2ax) = n\left(-\frac{39}{400}u^2\right)$$
$$1 = n\left(\frac{39}{400}\right) \implies n = \frac{400}{39} \approx 10.256$$
Thus, the least integer number of planks required is 11.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The relation between position $x$ and time $t$ of a particle moving along a straight line is given by $t = \alpha x^2 + \beta x$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants. The acceleration of the particle is:
questions.solution:
Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$:
$$1 = 2\alpha x \frac{dx}{dt} + \beta \frac{dx}{dt} = v(2\alpha x + \beta) \implies v = \frac{1}{2\alpha x + \beta}$$
Differentiating velocity with respect to time:
$$a = \frac{dv}{dt} = -\frac{1}{(2\alpha x + \beta)^2} \cdot 2\alpha \frac{dx}{dt} = -v^2 \cdot 2\alpha v = -2\alpha v^3$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A body is released from a height $h$. The ratio of distances travelled by the body in the $1^{\text{st}}$, $2^{\text{nd}}$ and $3^{\text{rd}}$ second of its motion is:
questions.solution:
Distance traversed in $n^{\text{th}}$ second for motion starting from rest ($u = 0$):
$$S_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n - 1) = \frac{g}{2}(2n - 1)$$
For $n = 1, 2, 3$:
$$S_1 : S_2 : S_3 = [2(1) - 1] : [2(2) - 1] : [2(3) - 1] = 1 : 3 : 5$$

questions.question: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity $v = \sqrt{4x + 16}$. The acceleration of the particle is:
questions.solution:
Squaring the velocity relation:
$$v^2 = 4x + 16$$
Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:
$$2v\frac{dv}{dx} = 4 \implies v\frac{dv}{dx} = 2$$
Since $a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$, the acceleration is constant and equals $2\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Two stones are thrown up simultaneously from the edge of a cliff $240\text{ m}$ high with initial speeds of $10\text{ m/s}$ and $40\text{ m/s}$ respectively. Which graph correctly represents the time variation of relative position of the second stone with respect to the first (taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)?
options: A straight line passing through origin up to $8\text{ s}$, then a parabolic curve up to $12\text{ s}$
A straight line up to $12\text{ s}$
A straight line up to $4\text{ s}$, then constant horizontal line
questions.solution:
For stone 1: $y_1 = 10t - 5t^2$. It strikes the ground when $y_1 = -240 \implies 5t^2 - 10t - 240 = 0 \implies t^2 - 2t - 48 = 0 \implies (t - 8)(t + 6) = 0 \implies t = 8\text{ s}$.
For stone 2: $y_2 = 40t - 5t^2$. It strikes the ground when $5t^2 - 40t - 240 = 0 \implies t^2 - 8t - 48 = 0 \implies t = 12\text{ s}$.
Between $0 \le t \le 8\text{ s}$, both stones are in flight: $y_2 - y_1 = (40t - 5t^2) - (10t - 5t^2) = 30t$ (a linear function through the origin).
For $8 < t \le 12\text{ s}$, stone 1 is stationary at the ground ($-240\text{ m}$): $y_2 - y_1 = (40t - 5t^2) - (-240) = 240 + 40t - 5t^2$ (a parabolic segment).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate $\alpha$ for some time, after which it decelerates at a constant rate $\beta$ to come to rest. If total time elapsed is $T$, then maximum velocity attained by the car is:
questions.solution:
Let acceleration last for time $t_1$ and deceleration last for time $t_2$. Then $t_1 + t_2 = T$.
Peak velocity $v_{\text{max}} = \alpha t_1 = \beta t_2$.
$$t_1 = \frac{v_{\text{max}}}{\alpha}, \quad t_2 = \frac{v_{\text{max}}}{\beta}$$
$$T = v_{\text{max}} \left(\frac{1}{\alpha} + \frac{1}{\beta}\right) = v_{\text{max}} \left(\frac{\alpha + \beta}{\alpha\beta}\right) \implies v_{\text{max}} = \frac{\alpha\beta}{\alpha + \beta} T$$

questions.question: A particle moves with uniform acceleration along a straight line $AB$. Its velocities at $A$ and $B$ are $u$ and $v$ respectively. If $C$ is the midpoint of $AB$, the velocity of the particle at $C$ is:
questions.solution:
Let the distance between $A$ and $B$ be $2s$, so distance $AC = CB = s$.
For section $AC$: $v_c^2 - u^2 = 2as \implies v_c^2 = u^2 + 2as$
For section $CB$: $v^2 - v_c^2 = 2as \implies v^2 - v_c^2 = v_c^2 - u^2$
$$2v_c^2 = u^2 + v^2 \implies v_c = \sqrt{\frac{u^2 + v^2}{2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A ball is dropped from a height of $100\text{ m}$. At the same instant, another ball is thrown upwards from the ground with a velocity of $50\text{ m/s}$. Both move along the same vertical line. The time after which the two balls meet is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
Consider relative motion between the two balls:
Relative acceleration $a_{\text{rel}} = (-g) - (-g) = 0$.
Relative velocity of approach $v_{\text{rel}} = u_2 - u_1 = 50 - 0 = 50\text{ m/s}$.
Initial separation $S_{\text{rel}} = 100\text{ m}$.
$$t = \frac{S_{\text{rel}}}{v_{\text{rel}}} = \frac{100}{50} = 2\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The position of an object is given by $x(t) = 8t - 3t^2$, where $x$ is in meters and $t$ is in seconds. The distance travelled by the object from $t = 0$ to $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Velocity is $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 8 - 6t$.
The particle stops when $v(t) = 0 \implies 8 - 6t = 0 \implies t = \frac{4}{3}\text{ s}$.
Since $t = \frac{4}{3}\text{ s}$ lies within $[0, 2]$, the direction of motion reverses.
Positions:
$x(0) = 0$
$x(4/3) = 8\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) - 3\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{32}{3} - \frac{16}{3} = \frac{16}{3}\text{ m}$
$x(2) = 8(2) - 3(4) = 16 - 12 = 4\text{ m}$
$$\text{Distance} = |x(4/3) - x(0)| + |x(2) - x(4/3)| = \frac{16}{3} + \left|4 - \frac{16}{3}\right| = \frac{16}{3} + \frac{4}{3} = \frac{20}{3}\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A particle starts from origin at $t = 0$ and moves along the positive x-axis. The graph of velocity with respect to position $x$ is a parabola with equation $v^2 = 4x$. The acceleration of the particle is:
questions.solution:
Differentiating the relation $v^2 = 4x$ with respect to $x$:
$$2v\frac{dv}{dx} = 4 \implies v\frac{dv}{dx} = 2$$
Since acceleration $a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$, we get $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.question: A balloon starts rising from the ground with an upward acceleration of $1.25\text{ m/s}^2$. After $8\text{ s}$, a stone is released from the balloon. The time taken by the stone to reach the ground is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
At $t = 8\text{ s}$:
Velocity of balloon $u = at = (1.25)(8) = 10\text{ m/s}$ (upward).
Height reached by balloon $h = \frac{1}{2}at^2 = \frac{1}{2}(1.25)(64) = 40\text{ m}$.
For the released stone:
Initial position $y_0 = 40\text{ m}$, initial velocity $u = +10\text{ m/s}$, $a = -10\text{ m/s}^2$.
When it strikes the ground ($y = 0$):
$$0 = 40 + 10t - 5t^2 \implies 5t^2 - 10t - 40 = 0 \implies t^2 - 2t - 8 = 0$$
$$(t - 4)(t + 2) = 0 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A train of length $200\text{ m}$ is moving with a constant speed of $20\text{ m/s}$. A bird starts flying from the back of the train to the front engine at a speed of $30\text{ m/s}$ relative to the ground, and returns back to the tail at the same speed. The total time taken by the bird for the round trip is:
questions.solution:
1) While moving from rear to front:
Relative speed $v_1 = 30 - 20 = 10\text{ m/s}$.
Time $t_1 = \frac{L}{v_1} = \frac{200}{10} = 20\text{ s}$.
2) While moving from front to rear:
Relative speed $v_2 = 30 + 20 = 50\text{ m/s}$.
Time $t_2 = \frac{L}{v_2} = \frac{200}{50} = 4\text{ s}$.
$$\text{Total time } T = t_1 + t_2 = 20 + 4 = 24\text{ s}$$

questions.question: A body is dropped from the top of a tower of height $H$. It covers a distance of $\frac{9H}{25}$ in the last second of its fall. The height $H$ of the tower is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
Total time of fall $T = \sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}$.
Distance fallen in the last second is:
$$S_{\text{last}} = \frac{g}{2}(2T - 1) = \frac{9}{25}H$$
Since $H = \frac{1}{2}gT^2$:
$$\frac{g}{2}(2T - 1) = \frac{9}{25}\left(\frac{1}{2}gT^2\right) \implies 2T - 1 = \frac{9}{25}T^2$$
$$9T^2 - 50T + 25 = 0 \implies (9T - 5)(T - 5) = 0$$
Since $T > 1\text{ s}$, we have $T = 5\text{ s}$.
$$H = \frac{1}{2}gT^2 = \frac{1}{2}(10)(25) = 125\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A particle moves in a straight line with deceleration proportional to its displacement. The loss of kinetic energy for any displacement $x$ is proportional to:
questions.solution:
Given $a = v\frac{dv}{dx} = -kx$.
$$v\,dv = -kx\,dx$$
Integrating from initial velocity $u$ to velocity $v$ over displacement $x$:
$$\int_u^v v\,dv = -k \int_0^x x\,dx \implies \frac{v^2 - u^2}{2} = -\frac{kx^2}{2}$$
$$\Delta K = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2) = -\frac{1}{2}mkx^2$$
Hence, the loss in kinetic energy is proportional to $x^2$.

questions.question: The velocity-time graph of a linear motion is shown. If the velocity is positive along the x-direction, the area under the $v-t$ curve with signs represents:
questions.solution:
By definition of velocity $v = \frac{dx}{dt}$, the integral with signs $\int v\,dt$ gives the displacement $\Delta x$.
The absolute sum of the areas $\int |v|\,dt$ would give the total distance.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A ball is thrown vertically upwards with speed $u$. If it passes a point at height $h$ above the projection point at times $t_1$ and $t_2$, then $t_1 + t_2$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The displacement equation is $h = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$, which rearranges to:
$$\frac{1}{2}gt^2 - ut + h = 0 \implies gt^2 - 2ut + 2h = 0$$
The roots of this quadratic equation are the two times $t_1$ and $t_2$ at which the ball is at height $h$.
By Vieta's formulas, sum of roots is:
$$t_1 + t_2 = -\frac{-2u}{g} = \frac{2u}{g}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An elevator is descending with an acceleration of $2\text{ m/s}^2$. A person in the elevator drops a coin from a height of $1.6\text{ m}$ above the elevator floor. The time taken by the coin to hit the floor is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
In the frame of reference of the elevator:
Initial relative velocity of the coin $u_{\text{rel}} = 0$.
Relative acceleration of the coin $a_{\text{rel}} = g - a_{\text{lift}} = 10 - 2 = 8\text{ m/s}^2$ (downwards).
Using $s = \frac{1}{2} a_{\text{rel}} t^2$:
$$1.6 = \frac{1}{2}(8)t^2 = 4t^2 \implies t^2 = \frac{1.6}{4} = 0.4 \implies t = \sqrt{0.4}\text{ s} \approx 0.632\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A car travels the first third of a journey with a speed of $10\text{ km/h}$, the second third with $20\text{ km/h}$, and the last third with $60\text{ km/h}$. The average speed of the car for the entire journey is $v\text{ km/h}$. Find the value of $v$.
questions.solution:
Let total distance be $3s$. Each section is of distance $s$.
Times taken for each section:
$t_1 = \frac{s}{10}$, $t_2 = \frac{s}{20}$, $t_3 = \frac{s}{60}$.
$$t_{\text{total}} = s\left(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{60}\right) = s\left(\frac{6 + 3 + 1}{60}\right) = s\left(\frac{10}{60}\right) = \frac{s}{6}$$
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{3s}{t_{\text{total}}} = \frac{3s}{s/6} = 18\text{ km/h}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A ball is dropped from a height $h = 45\text{ m}$. After striking the ground, it rebounds with a speed equal to $\frac{2}{3}$ of its striking speed. Find the maximum height (in meters) reached by the ball after the bounce (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
Velocity just before striking ground:
$$v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 45} = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ m/s}$$
Velocity immediately after rebound:
$$v' = \frac{2}{3}v = \frac{2}{3}(30) = 20\text{ m/s}$$
Maximum rebound height:
$$h' = \frac{v'^2}{2g} = \frac{20^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{400}{20} = 20\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A particle starts from the origin with an initial velocity $u = 5\text{ m/s}$ along the x-axis and moves with constant acceleration $a = -2\text{ m/s}^2$. The total distance travelled by the particle in the first $4\text{ s}$ of its motion is $d\text{ m}$. Find the value of $d$ (expressed in meters).
questions.solution:
The particle comes to a momentary stop when $v = 0$:
$$v = u + at \implies 0 = 5 - 2t \implies t = 2.5\text{ s}$$
Since $t = 2.5\text{ s}$ lies within the interval $[0, 4\text{ s}]$, motion reverses direction.
1) Distance covered during $0$ to $2.5\text{ s}$:
$$s_1 = \frac{u^2}{2|a|} = \frac{5^2}{2(2)} = \frac{25}{4} = 6.25\text{ m}$$
2) Distance covered during $2.5\text{ s}$ to $4\text{ s}$ (interval $\Delta t = 1.5\text{ s}$ starting from rest):
$$s_2 = \frac{1}{2}|a|(\Delta t)^2 = \frac{1}{2}(2)(1.5)^2 = 2.25\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Total distance } d = s_1 + s_2 = 6.25 + 2.25 = 8.5\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two trains $A$ and $B$, each of length $150\text{ m}$, are travelling on parallel tracks in opposite directions with uniform speeds of $36\text{ km/h}$ and $54\text{ km/h}$ respectively. The time taken (in seconds) for them to completely cross each other is:
questions.solution:
Speeds in SI units:
$v_A = 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\text{ m/s}$
$v_B = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\text{ m/s}$
Relative speed when moving in opposite directions:
$$v_{\text{rel}} = v_A + v_B = 10 + 15 = 25\text{ m/s}$$
Total relative distance to clear each other:
$$s_{\text{rel}} = L_A + L_B = 150 + 150 = 300\text{ m}$$
$$t = \frac{s_{\text{rel}}}{v_{\text{rel}}} = \frac{300}{25} = 12\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement from origin is given by $x = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2$ (where $x$ is in meters and $t$ in seconds). Find the magnitude of acceleration (in $\text{m/s}^2$) of the particle at the instant when its velocity is zero for the second time.
questions.solution:
Velocity of the particle is:
$$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 3t^2 - 12t + 9$$
Setting $v = 0$:
$$3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 0 \implies 3(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0$$
Velocity is zero at $t = 1\text{ s}$ and for the second time at $t = 3\text{ s}$.
Acceleration of the particle:
$$a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 6t - 12$$
At $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$a = 6(3) - 12 = 18 - 12 = 6\text{ m/s}^2$$
